map_to_spe <- function(data, k) {
  samples <- c("BALBc-1", "MRL-4")
  keep <- as.character(data$sample) %in% samples
  data <- data[keep, , drop = FALSE]
  display_spe <- SpatialExperiment::SpatialExperiment(
    assays = list(display = matrix(0, nrow = 1L, ncol = nrow(data))),
    colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(
      sample_id = factor(
        as.character(data$sample), levels = samples,
        labels = c("BALBc-1", "MRL-4 (early)")
      ),
      domain = factor(data$domain, levels = seq.int(0L, k - 1L))
    ),
    spatialCoords = as.matrix(data[, c("x", "y")]),
    sample_id = factor(
      as.character(data$sample), levels = samples,
      labels = c("BALBc-1", "MRL-4 (early)")
    )
  )
  display_spe
}

matrix_long <- function(x, value_name, condition = NULL) {
  result <- as.data.frame(as.table(as.matrix(x)), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  names(result) <- c("source", "target", value_name)
  if (!is.null(condition)) result$condition <- condition
  result
}

plot_enrichment_dotplot <- function(enrichment, k) {
  values <- as.matrix(enrichment$enrichment)
  size_threshold <- 0.58
  color_threshold <- 0.58

  # CellCharter v0.2.0 defaults to cluster_labels=TRUE. Its complete-linkage
  # clustering uses the thresholded color matrix, not the raw enrichment.
  color_values <- ifelse(
    values < 0, -1,
    ifelse(values < color_threshold, 0, 1)
  )
  domain_order <- colnames(values)
  if (ncol(values) > 1L) {
    domain_order <- domain_order[stats::hclust(
      stats::dist(t(color_values)), method = "complete"
    )$order]
  }

  cells <- expand.grid(
    cell_type = rownames(values), domain = colnames(values),
    KEEP.OUT.ATTRS = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  cells$value <- as.vector(values)
  # CellCharter maps [-1, 0.58] through TwoSlopeNorm. Scanpy 1.9.3 then
  # clips negative dot-size fractions to zero and uses area = fraction^1.5.
  # Base R `cex` scales diameter, hence exponent 1.5 / 2 = 0.75 here.
  cells$size <- pmax(0, pmin(cells$value, size_threshold)) / size_threshold
  cells$color_value <- as.vector(color_values)
  palette <- grDevices::colorRampPalette(
    c("#3B4CC0", "darkgrey", "#B40426")
  )(101)
  color_index <- pmax(
    1L, pmin(101L, round((cells$color_value + 1) * 50) + 1L)
  )
  graphics::plot(
    as.integer(factor(cells$cell_type, levels = rownames(values))),
    as.integer(factor(cells$domain, levels = domain_order)),
    pch = 21, bg = palette[color_index], col = "black",
    cex = 2.5 * cells$size^0.75, axes = FALSE,
    xlim = c(0.5, nrow(values) + 9),
    xlab = "", ylab = "Spatial domain (complete-linkage order)",
    main = paste0("Cluster ~ full cell type enrichment (K=", k, ")")
  )
  graphics::axis(
    1, at = seq_len(nrow(values)), labels = rownames(values),
    las = 2, cex.axis = 1
  )
  graphics::axis(
    2, at = seq_along(domain_order), labels = domain_order, las = 1
  )
  graphics::box()
  graphics::mtext("Cell type", side = 1, line = 16)
  graphics::legend(
    x = nrow(values) + 1, y = max(seq_along(domain_order)), xjust = 0,
    legend = c("depleted", "positive < 0.58", "enriched >= 0.58"),
    pt.bg = c("#3B4CC0", "darkgrey", "#B40426"),
    pch = 21, cex = 1, title = "log2 observed/expected", bty = "n"
  )
}

plot_heatmap <- function(x, title, limits = NULL, annotate = FALSE,
                         pvalue = NULL, significance = NULL) {
  x <- as.matrix(x)
  plotted <- x
  plotted[!is.finite(plotted)] <- NA_real_
  if (is.null(limits)) {
    limits <- range(plotted, finite = TRUE)
  }
  if (length(limits) != 2L || any(!is.finite(limits)) || limits[[1L]] >= 0 ||
      limits[[2L]] <= 0) {
    stop("Heatmap limits must be finite and span zero, as required by TwoSlopeNorm.")
  }
  palette <- grDevices::hcl.colors(101, "Blue-Red 3", rev = TRUE)
  graphics::image(
    seq_len(ncol(plotted)), seq_len(nrow(plotted)), t(plotted),
    col = palette, zlim = limits, axes = FALSE,
    xlab = "target domain", ylab = "source domain", main = title,
    useRaster = TRUE
  )
  graphics::axis(
    1, at = seq_len(ncol(plotted)), labels = colnames(plotted), las = 2
  )
  graphics::axis(
    2, at = seq_len(nrow(plotted)), labels = rownames(plotted), las = 2
  )
  graphics::box()
  if (annotate) {
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(plotted))) for (j in seq_len(ncol(plotted))) {
      if (!is.finite(plotted[i, j])) next
      significant <- !is.null(pvalue) && !is.null(significance) &&
        is.finite(pvalue[i, j]) && pvalue[i, j] <= significance
      label <- paste0(sprintf("%.2f", plotted[i, j]), if (significant) "*" else "")
      graphics::text(j, i, label, cex = 1)
    }
  }
}
```

> **Scope and provenance.** This preserved report starts from the fixed
> published trVAE representation and reproduces the downstream graph,
> aggregation, AutoK/GMM, enrichment, and proximity stages. It is not a claim
> of end-to-end representation equivalence. Every domain figure and downstream
> result in this report was generated from the completed compiled C++ CPU run.
> R Torch/CUDA remains available as an experimental alternative.

> **Static report.** The installed HTML is self-contained scientific evidence.
> Its source is archival and expects the preserved result directory named in
> `params$result_dir`; it is not intended to rerun a full-data analysis during
> package installation.

This is the second CellCharterR tutorial and the complete scientific
reproduction report. New users should first read the
[beginner workflow](https://cperalta-viteri.github.io/CellCharterR/docs/CellCharterR-beginner-workflow.html).
The next tutorial demonstrates
[additional downstream analyses](https://cperalta-viteri.github.io/CellCharterR/docs/CellCharterR-differential-neighborhood-networks.html)
from the preserved C++ K=10 result.

# Scope and artifact roles

This report consumes the completed compiled-C++ outputs. Earlier provisional
outputs are not used here. The
primary result is K=10, selected independently by the compiled C++ AutoK run
over the predeclared range K=2 through K=20. The K=11 panel is a separate
compiled C++ sensitivity fit corresponding to the tutorial's requested
resolution and seed 12345. The C++ and Python implementations use different
initialization and random-number streams, so this does not claim seed-identical
fitted parameters. Published H5AD `cluster_cellcharter` labels are not plotted
as either R result.

## Full mouse-spleen before/after benchmark

```{r full-benchmark, echo=TRUE}
format_duration <- function(seconds) {
  hours <- floor(seconds / 3600)
  minutes <- floor((seconds %% 3600) / 60)
  secs <- round(seconds %% 60)
  sprintf("%dh %02dm %02ds", hours, minutes, secs)
}

benchmark_table <- data.frame(
  implementation = c(
    manifest$benchmark$legacy$backend,
    manifest$benchmark$cpp$backend
  ),
  spatial_spots = format(manifest$benchmark$spots, big.mark = ","),
  features = manifest$benchmark$features,
  AutoK_rounds = manifest$benchmark$rounds,
  GMM_fits = manifest$benchmark$fits,
  observed_wall_time = c(
    paste0(">= ", format_duration(
      manifest$benchmark$legacy$elapsed_lower_bound_seconds
    )),
    format_duration(manifest$benchmark$cpp$elapsed_seconds)
  ),
  execution = c(
    paste0(manifest$benchmark$legacy$device, "; sequential K fits"),
    paste0(
      manifest$benchmark$cpp$workers, " workers x ",
      manifest$benchmark$cpp$threads_per_fit, " threads"
    )
  ),
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(
  benchmark_table,
  caption = "Observed timing for the same first five AutoK rounds (K=1 through K=21)"
)
```

For 707,474 spatial spots and 40 aggregated features, the compiled C++ run
completed the same 105-fit, five-round comparison window at least
`r sprintf("%.1f", manifest$benchmark$speedup_lower_bound)` times faster. The
legacy time is a conservative lower bound reconstructed from completed
checkpoint timestamps, whereas the C++ duration was recorded by the runner.
This is an observed workflow comparison, not a controlled microbenchmark: the
backends use different initializers and numerical engines. The comparison is
therefore evidence of the practical wall-time improvement, not a claim that
both optimizers produce identical fitted parameters.

# From input SPE to saved results

The full mouse-spleen analysis is deliberately not rerun while this report is
rendered. The code below shows the public stages used to create the graph,
in-memory neighborhood representation, AutoK fit, selected domains, and
downstream statistics. The evaluated sections that follow load the corresponding
precomputed artifacts and display their outputs.

## CPU threading required by the parallel C++ backend

CellCharterR schedules `workers` simultaneous fits and gives each fit
`threads_per_fit` threads. The linked BLAS must use one thread so it does not
create another thread pool inside every fit. Without this restriction, nested
oversubscription can exhaust CPU and memory bandwidth and make fitting much
slower.

Before starting R, add the following entries to the analysis project's
`.Renviron` file (use `file.edit(".Renviron")` in RStudio), save it, and restart
R:

```text
OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1
OMP_NUM_THREADS=1
MKL_NUM_THREADS=1
BLIS_NUM_THREADS=1
VECLIB_MAXIMUM_THREADS=1
GOTO_NUM_THREADS=1
```

This restricts BLAS/OpenMP nesting, not CellCharterR itself. The call below can
still use up to `workers * threads_per_fit` threads. Verify that all six values
are `"1"` before loading CellCharterR:

```{r verify-cpu-thread-environment, eval=FALSE}
Sys.getenv(c(
  "OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS", "OMP_NUM_THREADS", "MKL_NUM_THREADS",
  "BLIS_NUM_THREADS", "VECLIB_MAXIMUM_THREADS", "GOTO_NUM_THREADS"
))
```

```{r full-staged-workflow, eval=FALSE}
full_spe <- readRDS("results/CellCharterR_mouse_spleen_v2/representation/codex_sce.rds")

full_spe <- cellcharter_graph(
  full_spe,
  spatial = "spatial",
  sample_col = "sample",
  graph_name = "cellcharter_graph",
  percentile = 99
)

full_spe <- cellcharter_aggregate(
  full_spe,
  representation = "X_trVAE",
  graph_name = "cellcharter_graph",
  sample_col = "sample",
  output = "X_cellcharter",
  n_layers = 3L
)

saveRDS(
  full_spe,
  "results/CellCharterR_mouse_spleen_v2/aggregation/spe_after_aggregation.rds",
  compress = FALSE
)

full_spe <- cellcharter_cluster(
  full_spe,
  representation = "X_cellcharter",
  candidate_k = c(2L, 20L),
  checkpoint_dir = "results/CellCharterR_mouse_spleen_cpp_v1/unused-no-checkpoints",
  domain_col = "cellcharter_domain",
  max_runs = 10L,
  convergence_tol = 0.01,
  seed = 0L,
  backend = "cpp",
  workers = 8L,
  threads_per_fit = 4L,
  checkpoint_mode = "none",
  fit_args = list(
    max_iter = 100L,
    tolerance = 0.001,
    covariance_regularization = 1e-6
  ),
  resume = FALSE
)

full_spe <- cellcharter_enrichment(
  full_spe,
  group_col = "cell_type",
  domain_col = "cellcharter_domain"
)
full_spe <- cellcharter_nhood_enrichment(
  full_spe,
  graph_name = "cellcharter_graph",
  domain_col = "cellcharter_domain"
)
full_spe <- cellcharter_diff_nhood_enrichment(
  full_spe,
  graph_name = "cellcharter_graph",
  domain_col = "cellcharter_domain",
  condition_col = "condition",
  sample_col = "sample",
  condition_groups = c("BALBc", "MRL"),
  n_perms = 100L,
  seed = 0L,
  permutation_mode = "cellcharter_v0.2.0"
)

saveRDS(
  full_spe,
  "results/CellCharterR_mouse_spleen_v2/downstream/codex_spe_complete.rds"
)
```

## Optional resumable compiled C++ run

The measured 38-minute run above used `checkpoint_mode = "none"` to avoid all
fit-checkpoint I/O. If interruption recovery is more important, use a new
directory and `checkpoint_mode = "round"`; repeat this exact call with
`resume = TRUE` after an interruption.

```{r full-resume-workflow, eval=FALSE}
full_spe <- readRDS(
  "results/CellCharterR_mouse_spleen_v2/aggregation/spe_after_aggregation.rds"
)

full_spe <- cellcharter_cluster(
  full_spe,
  representation = "X_cellcharter",
  candidate_k = c(2L, 20L),
  checkpoint_dir = "results/CellCharterR_mouse_spleen_cpp_resumable/autok",
  domain_col = "cellcharter_domain",
  max_runs = 10L,
  convergence_tol = 0.01,
  seed = 0L,
  backend = "cpp",
  workers = 8L,
  threads_per_fit = 4L,
  checkpoint_mode = "round",
  fit_args = list(
    max_iter = 100L, tolerance = 0.001,
    covariance_regularization = 1e-6
  ),
  resume = TRUE
)
```

The resume call is deliberately identical to the original fit call. Changing
the backend, seed, candidate range, or numerical settings creates a different
fit contract and must use a new checkpoint directory.

## Optional compact wrapper

For a compact dataset, `cellcharter_workflow()` composes the same stages. It is
shown for completeness, but the staged version above is preferable for the full
dataset because it exposes each durable checkpoint. If aggregation exceeds
available RAM, add `filepath = ...` and retain that optional HDF5 file with the SPE.

```{r full-workflow-wrapper, eval=FALSE}
full_spe <- cellcharter_workflow(
  full_spe,
  group_col = "cell_type",
  candidate_k = c(2L, 20L),
  checkpoint_dir = "results/CellCharterR_mouse_spleen_cpp_v1/unused-no-checkpoints",
  representation = "X_trVAE",
  sample_col = "sample",
  condition_col = "condition",
  aggregated = "X_cellcharter",
  domain_col = "cellcharter_domain",
  n_layers = 3L,
  condition_groups = c("BALBc", "MRL"),
  n_perms = 100L,
  seed = 0L,
  autok_args = list(
    backend = "cpp",
    workers = 8L,
    threads_per_fit = 4L,
    checkpoint_mode = "none",
    fit_args = list(
      max_iter = 100L, tolerance = 0.001,
      covariance_regularization = 1e-6
    )
  )
)
```


# AutoK stability and K selection

The points are all saved neighboring-K Fowlkes--Mallows comparisons from the
five repeated fits; the line is their mean. AutoK stopped before the requested
maximum of ten runs because the final stability change was 0.00793, below the
predeclared `convergence_tol = 0.01`. K=1 is shown as non-estimable
because this criterion requires fitted solutions on both neighboring K values.
K=10 is the independently selected global maximum. Other local peaks remain
visible because stability is a resolution diagnostic, not a command to ignore
biologically useful alternatives. K=11 is annotated as the predeclared
tutorial-matched sensitivity on the neighboring stability shoulder.

```{r autok-stability, echo=TRUE, out.width="100%", fig.cap="Compiled C++ neighboring-K Fowlkes--Mallows stability for the full mouse-spleen analysis. K=10 is the independently selected primary resolution; K=11 is highlighted as the tutorial-matched sensitivity resolution, while other local peaks remain visible.", fig.alt="Mouse-spleen compiled C++ neighboring-K Fowlkes-Mallows stability from K 2 through K 20; K 10 is selected, K 11 is highlighted, and other peaks remain visible"}
knitr::include_graphics(manifest$autok_stability_plot)
```

## Differential neighborhood enrichment in both display directions

Both panels reuse one sample-level permutation result (`n_perms=100`). A star
marks directional empirical `p <= 0.05`; reversing the display negates only the
effect and reuses the same permutation counts and p-values.

```{r primary-differential, echo=TRUE, fig.width=12, fig.height=5.5, fig.cap="Compiled C++ primary K=10 differential directed neighborhood enrichment in both MRL-minus-BALBc and BALBc-minus-MRL display directions.", fig.alt="Compiled C++ primary K 10 differential directed neighborhood enrichment shown as MRL minus BALBc and the reversed BALBc minus MRL display"}
graphics::par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(5, 5, 3, 1))
plot_heatmap(
  primary_mrl_balbc$effect, "MRL vs BALBc", annotate = TRUE,
  pvalue = primary_mrl_balbc$pvalue, significance = 0.05
)
plot_heatmap(
  primary_balbc_mrl$effect, "BALBc vs MRL", annotate = TRUE,
  pvalue = primary_balbc_mrl$pvalue, significance = 0.05
)
```

```{r primary-differential-table, echo=TRUE, eval=FALSE}

knitr::kable(primary_diff_table,
             caption = "Values underlying the primary differential heatmaps")
```

# Standalone tutorial-matched K=11 sensitivity analysis

The C++ K=11 sensitivity was one standalone fit, not an AutoK selection and not
the published H5AD labels. These are the exact historical settings used to
generate its preserved labels:

```{r k11-fit-code, eval=FALSE}
full_spe <- cellcharter_cluster_fixed(
  full_spe,
  representation = "X_cellcharter",
  n_clusters = 11L,
  domain_col = "cellcharter_domain_k11_sensitivity",
  checkpoint_dir = "results/CellCharterR_mouse_spleen_v2/tutorial_k11_standalone",
  seed = 12345L,
  fit_args = list(
    max_iter = 100L,
    tolerance = 0.001,
    covariance_regularization = 1e-6,
    num_threads = 4L
  ),
  predict_args = list(),
  fit_fun = cpp_gmm_fit,
  predict_fun = cpp_gmm_predict,
  resume = TRUE
)
```

```{r k11-load, echo=TRUE}
k11_paths <- manifest$artifacts$TutorialK11
k11_map <- readRDS(k11_paths[["map_input"]])
k11_enrichment <- readRDS(k11_paths[["enrichment"]])
k11_nhood <- readRDS(k11_paths[["nhood"]])
k11_mrl_balbc <- readRDS(k11_paths[["differential_mrl_balbc"]])
k11_balbc_mrl <- readRDS(k11_paths[["differential_balbc_mrl"]])
```

## BALBc-1 and early MRL-4 domains

```{r k11-maps, echo=TRUE, fig.width=12, fig.height=5.5, fig.cap="Tutorial-matched K=11 sensitivity domains in the BALBc-1 and early MRL-4 slides.", fig.alt="K=11 sensitivity spatial domains on BALBc-1 and early MRL-4"}
k11_spe <- map_to_spe(k11_map, 11L)
ggspavis::plotCoords(
  k11_spe,
  annotate = "domain",
  sample_id = "sample_id",
  in_tissue = NULL,
  point_size = 0.1,
  pal = grDevices::hcl.colors(11L, "Dynamic")
) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    colour = "Domain",
    title = "Tutorial-matched sensitivity spatial domains: K = 11"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 16)
```

```{r k11-map-table, echo=TRUE, eval=FALSE}
knitr::kable(
  as.data.frame(table(sample = k11_map$sample, domain = k11_map$domain)),
  caption = "Accessible spot counts underlying the K=11 domain maps"
)
```

## Cluster ~ full cell type dot plot (log2 observed/expected)

```{r k11-dotplot, echo=TRUE, fig.width=18, fig.height=10, fig.cap="Positive cell-type enrichment in the tutorial-matched K=11 sensitivity domains. Darker and larger red points indicate stronger positive log2 fold change.", fig.alt="Positive cell-type enrichment by K=11 sensitivity domain; darker and larger red points indicate stronger positive log2 fold change"}
graphics::par(mar = c(18, 6, 3, 1))
CellCharterR::cellcharter_plot_enrichment(
  k11_enrichment,
  title = "Cluster ~ full cell type enrichment (K=11)"
)
```

```{r k11-dotplot-table, echo=TRUE, eval=FALSE}
k11_enrichment_table <- as.data.frame(
  as.table(k11_enrichment$enrichment), stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
names(k11_enrichment_table) <- c("cell_type", "domain", "log2_enrichment")
knitr::kable(k11_enrichment_table,
             caption = "Values underlying the K=11 enrichment dot plot")
```

## BALBc and MRL neighborhood enrichment

```{r k11-nhood, echo=TRUE, fig.width=14, fig.height=7, fig.cap="Directed observed-minus-expected neighborhood enrichment for BALBc and MRL at the K=11 sensitivity resolution.", fig.alt="Directed observed-minus-expected neighborhood enrichment for BALBc and MRL at K=11"}
graphics::par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(5, 5, 3, 1))
plot_heatmap(
  k11_nhood$BALBc$enrichment, "Healthy spleen — BALBc (K=11)",
  limits = c(-1, 1), annotate = TRUE
)
plot_heatmap(
  k11_nhood$MRL$enrichment, "Systemic lupus — MRL (K=11)",
  limits = c(-1, 1), annotate = TRUE
)
```

```{r k11-nhood-table, echo=TRUE, eval=FALSE}
k11_nhood_table <- rbind(
  matrix_long(k11_nhood$BALBc$enrichment, "enrichment", "BALBc"),
  matrix_long(k11_nhood$MRL$enrichment, "enrichment", "MRL")
)
knitr::kable(k11_nhood_table,
             caption = "Values underlying the K=11 neighborhood heatmaps")
```

## Differential neighborhood enrichment in both display directions

```{r k11-differential, echo=TRUE, fig.width=15, fig.height=7.5, fig.cap="K=11 sensitivity differential directed neighborhood enrichment in both MRL-minus-BALBc and BALBc-minus-MRL display directions.", fig.alt="K=11 differential directed neighborhood enrichment shown as MRL minus BALBc and the reversed display"}
graphics::par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(5, 5, 3, 1))
plot_heatmap(
  k11_mrl_balbc$effect, "MRL vs BALBc (K=11)", annotate = TRUE,
  pvalue = k11_mrl_balbc$pvalue, significance = 0.05
)
plot_heatmap(
  k11_balbc_mrl$effect, "BALBc vs MRL (K=11)", annotate = TRUE,
  pvalue = k11_balbc_mrl$pvalue, significance = 0.05
)
```

```{r k11-differential-table, echo=TRUE, eval=FALSE}
k11_diff_table <- matrix_long(k11_mrl_balbc$effect, "MRL_minus_BALBc")
k11_diff_table$empirical_pvalue <- as.vector(k11_mrl_balbc$pvalue)
knitr::kable(k11_diff_table,
             caption = "Values underlying the K=11 differential heatmaps")
```

# Interpretation boundary

The R-selected AutoK K remains the only primary result. K=11 is a separately
fitted tutorial sensitivity analysis. The published H5AD labels remain a
separate reference artifact. Representation-learning equivalence is not claimed
because the supplied trVAE representation is treated as immutable input.
Spatial panels use `ggspavis::plotCoords()` on `SpatialExperiment` objects with
the exact saved coordinates and labels. Pixel-level equivalence to Squidpy's
plotting stack is not claimed.
